technical_and_design_decisions: Each ported module (U1–U5) will be implemented as a Spring Cloud Stream Processor conforming to the standard reactive `Function<Message<?>, Message<?>>` / `Function<Flux<Message<?>>, Flux<Message<?>>>` pattern used in s-c-s.
Modules will reuse the existing Spring Cloud Stream test binder (`MessageCollector`) for integration tests, avoiding the need for an external broker during unit/integration testing.

The BinderFactory (U8) will be modeled after the existing `BindableProxyFactory` / `ChannelFactory` patterns, exposing a `getBinder(String name, Class<?> bindableType)` lookup API that allows registering multiple binder implementations (e.g., Kafka, Rabbit, Kinesis) at runtime.
Exploration stories U6 and U7 are scoped to produce design notes / proposal documents (Spike outcomes) rather than production code, per the 'explore options' wording.
Code will follow the Spring Framework coding conventions (checkstyle, JavaDoc on public APIs) and target Java 17 as required by Spring Framework 6.0+.
Script module (U3) will leverage the existing `ResourceScriptExecutor` abstraction to support Groovy/JavaScript/etc. with configurable engine order.
Shell module (U4) will wrap process execution using `ProcessBuilder` with timeout/cancellation hooks integrated with the reactive subscription lifecycle.
Splitter module (U5) will default to the Spring Integration `AbstractMessageSplitter` semantics with a configurable SpEL expression for partition criteria.
assumptions: The developer has working knowledge of both Spring XD internals and the target Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s) repository layout; no ramp-up on framework fundamentals is included.
Reference implementations of the XD modules (json-to-tuple, object-to-json, script, shell, splitter) are accessible and well-documented in the Spring XD codebase.

A standard workday of 8 hours is used; estimates cover development, unit tests, light integration tests, code review rework, and basic JavaDoc — not multi-party design workshops or extended stakeholder reviews.
Build/CI plumbing (Maven, dependency snapshots, test-binder) in s-c-s is already in place; only module-specific additions to `pom.xml` files are accounted for.
Existing utility classes (e.g., JSON conversion helpers, tuple serialization) in s-c-s are available and can be reused instead of re-implemented from scratch.
Each user story is treated as independent deliverable work; dependencies between them are limited to shared build config, which is captured in the setup activity.
Exploration stories (U6, U7) deliver written proposals (1–2 pages each) with feasibility notes and recommended next steps, not working code.
BinderFactory includes a single reference implementation proving the abstraction works, but adding new concrete binders (Kafka/Rabbit/etc. migration) is out of scope.
A reactive-first approach is taken where the surrounding s-c-s APIs support it, but legacy `Message`-based signatures are preserved for backward compatibility within s-c-s 2.x/3.x.

activities.activity_name: Project setup, source analysis and design alignment
activities.activity_description: Review the five XD source modules, study the s-c-s Processor conventions, set up new Maven modules, and create a shared porting checklist / design notes used by all port activities.
Port the XD json-to-tuple module into s-c-s as a reactive Processor that converts a JSON payload into a Tuple, including unit tests and JavaDoc.
Port the XD object-to-json module into s-c-s as a reactive Processor that serializes a POJO payload to JSON, including configurable ObjectMapper options and tests.
Port the XD script module into s-c-s as a reactive Processor that delegates payload evaluation to a configurable script engine (Groovy, JavaScript, etc.), with engine-isolation and tests.

Port the XD shell module into s-c-s as a reactive Processor that invokes an external shell command per message, with timeout, cancellation, and stdout/stderr mapping to the output message, plus tests.
Port the XD splitter module into s-c-s as a reactive Processor that splits incoming messages into multiple outbound messages based on a SpEL/configurable expression, with tests.

activities.activity_name: Spike: explore options to remove composed job (U6)
activities.activity_description: Investigate composed-job usage in XD/SCDF, list candidates for removal, and produce a short design note with impact analysis, risks, and a recommended cleanup plan.

activities.activity_name: Spike: explore options to persist composed job definition in ZooKeeper (U7)
activities.activity_description: Investigate ZK metadata storage options for composed-job definitions, prototype a serialization approach, and document trade-offs (consistency, recovery semantics) in a design note.
Define the public API of the BinderFactory, integration points with the existing binder lifecycle, configuration metadata, and obtain a brief design review.
Implement the BinderFactory interface, default registry, name/type-based lookup, and wire it into the existing configuration mechanism.

activities.activity_name: Tests and reference binder for BinderFactory (U8 – test)
activities.activity_description: Write unit and integration tests for BinderFactory lookup, registration, and fallback behavior, and provide a simple in-memory reference binder that exercises the abstraction.
Wire the five ported processors into a sample Spring Cloud Data Flow streaming pipeline definition, run end-to-end tests using the test binder, and fix integration regressions.
Update s-c-s reference documentation with the new processor modules and BinderFactory usage, and add module-level README/Asciidoc snippets.
Address review feedback, run checkstyle/full test suite, fix remaining defects, and prepare the increment for merge.
